title: Hyperbolic lattices with mass disorder: Phases and phase transitions
authors: Sheersh Sen, Christopher A. Leong, Bitan Roy
abstract: Nearest-neighbor (NN) tight-binding models (TBMs) on plaquette-centered $\{ 10,3\}$ (Schläfli symbol), $\{ 8,3\}$, and $\{ 8,4\}$ hyperbolic lattices on a Poincaré disk with open boundary conditions display a vanishing, a finite, and a diverging density of states (DOS) near zero energy (band center), respectively, yielding a Dirac liquid, a Fermi liquid, and a flat band. Emergent bipartite nature of these lattices within the framework of NN-TBMs, allows us to scrutinize the impact of mass disorder on the electronic states and DOS therein. From extensive numerical calculations of the average and typical DOS using the kernel polynomial method, we show that hyperbolic Dirac liquid remains stable against weak mass disorder, undergoing a semimetal-to-metal quantum phase transition at moderate disorder, followed by an Anderson metal-to-insulator transition at even stronger disorder. The remaining two systems display only the latter transition. Critical exponents near all these transitions are found to be close to the ones mediated by on-site potential disorder.
summary: This paper analyzes the electronic properties of tight-binding models on hyperbolic lattices subjected to mass disorder. Using numerical methods like the Kernel Polynomial Method, the authors map out distinct quantum phase transitions, including semimetal-to-metal and Anderson metal-to-insulator transitions. The findings are crucial for understanding disorder effects in geometrically constrained quantum materials.
main_problem: The study investigates how mass disorder affects the electronic states and Density of States (DOS) in hyperbolic lattices.
main_result: The hyperbolic Dirac liquid remains stable against weak disorder, undergoing a semimetal-to-metal QPT, followed by an AMIT at stronger disorder, while other systems only show the AMIT.
method: The analysis employs the Kernel Polynomial Method (KPM) to compute both the average and typical Density of States (DOS) over multiple disorder realizations.
model_or_system: The system is based on Nearest-neighbor (NN) tight-binding models on specific hyperbolic lattices ($\{10, 3\}$, $\{8, 3\}$, and $\{8, 4\}$) embedded on a Poincaré disk. Mass disorder is introduced by assigning random on-site potentials to complementary sublattices.
key_observables: Average and typical Density of States ($ho_a(E), ho_t(E)$), and the critical exponents characterizing the phase transitions.
important_parameters: The disorder strength ($W$), which dictates the transition between semimetal, metal, and Anderson insulator phases.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the applicability of the tight-binding model framework and uses disorder averaging techniques (KPM) to characterize the bulk properties.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the DOS for the $\{10, 3\}$ lattice showing QPT and AMIT, and the DOS for $\{8, 3\}$ and $\{8, 4\}$ showing the AMIT. Scaling analyses are used to extract critical exponents.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the clean limit behavior (Dirac liquid, Fermi liquid, flat band) and then systematically analyzes the impact of mass disorder, detailing the sequence of quantum phase transitions observed for each lattice type.
why_interesting: The study provides a concrete example of how geometric constraints (hyperbolic curvature) interact with disorder to dictate complex quantum phase transitions, relevant for engineered photonic or electronic metamaterials.
